articles.title: "I was never home": Travis Kelce's mom Donna Kelce reveals the 20-year Thanksgiving sacrifice she made to support her son's football careers
articles.summary: For many families, Thanksgiving means gathering around a familiar dinner table, sharing a home-cooked meal and spending time together.
articles.body: For many families, Thanksgiving means gathering around a familiar dinner table, sharing a home-cooked meal and spending time together. Donna Kelce, however, spent nearly two decades celebrating the holiday differently. Her sons, Travis and Jason Kelce, had football commitments that often kept them away from home. Rather than wait for them to return, Donna made a habit of travelling to wherever they were playing. The family tradition offered a glimpse into the effort she made to stay close to her sons while their football careers continued to shape their lives.Donna Kelce travelled wherever Travis and Jason played footballDuring a November 2023 interview with Extra's Billy Bush, Donna Kelce opened up about how her sons' football schedules influenced their Thanksgiving celebrations. Travis was playing for the Kansas City Chiefs, while Jason was still an NFL centre for the Philadelphia Eagles. Their demanding schedules meant that a traditional holiday at home was rarely possible.Donna explained that she had followed her sons across different locations for years, including when they were still playing college football. Instead of asking them to change their schedules, she adjusted her own plans to make sure the family could spend time together."They're practicing. They're playing games on Sunday. I have always for the past, oh, 20 years gone to where they are, even in college. It was like, wherever they were, they were playing football… We were usually at either restaurants or at somebody’s house or something like that. I was never home. I’m never home on Thanksgiving. It is great, you don't have to cook."Her comments revealed that the tradition was not limited to the brothers' NFL careers. Donna had been doing the same thing since their college football days, making it a long-standing part of their family life.Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce's careers changed family celebrationsThe Kelce brothers' success brought them national attention, but their professional commitments also changed how the family marked important occasions. Thanksgiving became less about hosting a large dinner and more about finding a place where everyone could come together.Donna's lighthearted remark about not having to cook also showed how comfortably she had adapted to the arrangement. Rather than treating the changing plans as a problem, she found a practical way to make the holiday work.By travelling to her sons, Donna made family time possible without asking either brother to put his football responsibilities aside. It was a simple arrangement, but one that reflected the effort required to maintain family connections during demanding sporting careers.Her 2023 interview also offered a reminder that behind Travis and Jason's achievements was a mother who had spent years adjusting her own traditions to support them. Even as their careers took them to different cities, Donna continued to make Thanksgiving a family occasion.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “I remember it being difficult going to school": Gracie Hunt reveals the painful childhood reality of supporting the Chiefs in Cowboys territory
articles.summary: Growing up in Dallas was not always easy for Gracie Hunt, especially when football season arrived.
articles.body: Growing up in Dallas was not always easy for Gracie Hunt, especially when football season arrived. Her family belonged to the Kansas City Chiefs, but the city around her largely celebrated the Dallas Cowboys. At a time when Tony Romo was leading the Cowboys through successful seasons, the Chiefs were struggling to find their footing. That made Gracie stand out among her classmates. Years later, as Kansas City became one of the NFL's biggest forces, she looked back on those school days and the teasing that came with supporting her family's team.Gracie Hunt faced Cowboys fans while supporting the ChiefsGracie Hunt's connection to the Kansas City Chiefs began long before the franchise became a regular Super Bowl contender. As the daughter of Chiefs chairman and CEO Clark Hunt, football was already a major part of her family life. But growing up in Dallas meant she did not always share the same loyalties as her classmates.In a December 21, 2024, interview with Sports Illustrated, Gracie recalled what it was like supporting Kansas City in a city where the Cowboys attracted much of the attention.“I remember it being difficult going to school in Dallas when the Cowboys had Tony Romo, and were seeing some success,”Romo was a popular figure among Cowboys supporters during his time with the franchise. His success made the team's following even stronger, while Kansas City was still working through a difficult period.For Gracie, the situation meant dealing with a football rivalry that extended beyond game days. Her family connection to the Chiefs made her allegiance clear, even when the team did not enjoy the same success as its Texas rival.Gracie Hunt watches Dallas friends embrace Chiefs KingdomThe contrast between those school years and the Chiefs' current standing has been striking. Kansas City later built a championship-winning team under head coach Andy Reid, with Patrick Mahomes becoming the face of its success. The franchise's growing popularity also changed how people around Gracie viewed the team.She noticed that some of the same people who once supported Dallas had developed an interest in Kansas City.“I'd say that now, most of my friends are actually Chiefs fans here in Dallas — so Chiefs kingdom knows no bounds.”Her observation offered a lighthearted look at how dramatically the team's image had changed. The Chiefs were no longer struggling to earn attention. Their success had helped attract supporters well beyond Missouri, including in a city traditionally associated with the Cowboys.For Gracie, the change also made the memory of those school days more interesting. She had supported Kansas City when doing so was not the popular choice among her classmates. Now, with the Chiefs enjoying widespread recognition, she could see how much the team's fortunes had changed.Her story was a reminder that her connection to the franchise existed long before its recent championship era.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' $325 million KC Current gave 70+ charities a platform through its community initiative
articles.summary: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have helped build the Kansas City Current into one of the most talked-about clubs in women's soccer.
articles.body: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have helped build the Kansas City Current into one of the most talked-about clubs in women's soccer. But their involvement in the NWSL franchise has also created opportunities beyond the pitch. During the 2024 season, the club worked with United Way of Greater Kansas City to recognise more than 70 nonprofit organisations through its Waymakers of the Match programme. Instead of limiting community support to financial contributions, the initiative gave local charities something equally valuable: a chance to introduce their work to thousands of soccer fans.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current gave local charities a bigger platformThe Waymakers of the Match programme offered nonprofit organisations recognition during KC Current home matches. Through special events and matchday features, the club helped bring attention to groups working on different issues across the Kansas City region..For smaller charities, visibility can be difficult to secure. Many rely on limited resources and local supporters to keep their programmes running. Being recognised at a professional soccer match allowed these organisations to reach people who might not otherwise have heard about their work.The programme also gave supporters an opportunity to learn about community needs while attending games. It created a connection between the club's growing fan base and organisations working behind the scenes to help local residents.The initiative formed part of a wider relationship between KC Current and United Way of Greater Kansas City, which has worked with businesses, volunteers and nonprofit partners to address local challenges.How Patrick and Brittany Mahomes became part of KC Current's ownershipBrittany Mahomes was among the club's original owners when the franchise launched in 2020 alongside Angie and Chris Long. Patrick joined the ownership group in January 2023, becoming the first active NFL player to hold an ownership stake in an NWSL team.Brittany welcomed her husband's involvement and highlighted the work already taking place behind the scenes.“We are so thrilled to make this a family affair and have Patrick join as an owner,” said Brittany. “He has been a huge supporter behind-the-scenes. His passion for the Current is undeniable and I am glad that he will be with us as we continue on our journey to become the best in the NWSL."Patrick also expressed his excitement about joining the club's ownership team.“I am thankful for the chance to join my wife as part of the Kansas City Current’s ownership team,” Patrick said. “Brittany and the Longs have done an incredible job building a world-class organization. I am excited to join another championship-caliber club as it continues to make history.”The nonprofit recognition programme adds another dimension to the couple's involvement in women's soccer. articles.title: Alphonso Smith cause of death: Disturbing police report reveals details of former NFL cornerback’s final hours
articles.summary: The death of former NFL cornerback Alphonso Smith has taken a heartbreaking turn following the release of new details from the police investigation.
articles.body: The death of former NFL cornerback Alphonso Smith has taken a heartbreaking turn following the release of new details from the police investigation. Smith, who died at 40 in September 2026, had built a respected football career at Wake Forest before playing in the NFL. A newly disclosed account of his final hours has now raised further questions about the emotional struggles he may have faced. The report also offers a clearer picture of the events that led to his death, bringing renewed attention to the loss of the former Denver Broncos and Detroit Lions player.Alphonso Smith cause of death: Police report reveals disturbing detailsAccording to a report obtained by TMZ from the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, Smith was at a home in Pahokee, Florida, on September 2 when a woman became concerned about his behaviour.She reportedly heard him crying and praying while speaking with several people on a conference call. The woman attempted to comfort him and asked him to explain what was troubling him. However, Smith allegedly asked her to leave him alone and go upstairs.The mother of his children arrived shortly afterwards. Both women reportedly witnessed Smith shoot himself. Deputies reached the property and found him critically injured.Emergency responders took him to a nearby hospital before transferring him to St. Mary's Medical Center in Palm Beach County. He was pronounced dead at 3:19 p.m.The police report also mentioned the presence of THC in his system. However, its detection alone does not establish that cannabis played any role in the circumstances surrounding his death.Alphonso Smith’s emotional Facebook message and NFL careerAn emotional message shared on Smith's Facebook account shortly before his death has also drawn attention. In the post, he apologised to his family, children and friends while reflecting on painful experiences from his childhood."To my family, BABY, my MOM, my siblings, things happened to your boy, your brother while I was little that an older lady did onto me," he wrote. "As a result guys, I did the same onto others!""I am the WORST & I pray my soul rest in heaven for my heart is pure, but my BRAIN & experience is MESSED UP !!. Once again to ALLLLLL! I am SORRY! THIS IS IT!"Beyond the headlines surrounding his death, Smith leaves behind a notable football legacy. At Wake Forest, he recorded 21 career interceptions, an ACC record, and earned multiple All-American honours. He also helped the programme win the 2006 ACC Championship.The Denver Broncos selected him 37th overall in the 2009 NFL Draft. He later played for the Detroit Lions, appearing in 42 NFL games before his professional career ended in 2012.Smith finished with 88 tackles and eight interceptions, including two returned for touchdowns. Wake Forest confirmed his death on September 3, remembering him as one of the programme's standout defensive players.His passing is a reminder that emotional struggles can remain hidden even when someone has achieved success in public life. articles.title: Bengals star Tee Higgins pays heartfelt tribute to Fiona the hippo after her heartbreaking death
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals' latest game carried an emotional reminder of a beloved member of the city's community.
articles.body: The Cincinnati Bengals' latest game carried an emotional reminder of a beloved member of the city's community. Wide receiver Tee Higgins made sure Fiona the hippo was not forgotten, choosing a special outfit to honour the Cincinnati Zoo favourite following her death. His gesture came just days after the nine-year-old animal passed away, leaving zoo staff and fans heartbroken. Although the Bengals were playing away from home, Higgins found a way to show how deeply the loss had affected him and the city he represents.Tee Higgins honours Fiona the hippo with emotional pregame tributeHiggins arrived at Northwest Stadium in Maryland on November 23 ahead of the Bengals' Monday Night Football matchup against the Washington Commanders wearing a light blue sweatshirt featuring a large illustration of Fiona.The design included her name in bright yellow lettering, making the tribute easy to spot. Higgins completed his look with dark sweatpants, white sneakers, thick-framed glasses and a black backpack.The outfit was more than a fashion choice. It reflected the connection Fiona had built with Cincinnati residents, including people who had followed her remarkable story since birth.After Cincinnati's 22-20 defeat to Washington, Higgins explained why he decided to honour the hippo.“Obviously, Cincinnati is mourning pretty hard about that one and I felt it,” he told reporters in the locker room. “I love Cincinnati, so I just showed my love to the Cincinnati Zoo and Fiona.”His comments highlighted how Fiona's loss reached beyond the zoo. She had become a familiar face and a source of joy for people across the city.Fiona the hippo’s death leaves Cincinnati Zoo community heartbrokenFiona died on November 19 at the age of nine, around two weeks after swallowing a visitor's hat that had accidentally fallen into her enclosure. Her death shocked the Cincinnati Zoo, particularly because staff had hoped she would recover.“We are in shock at the moment,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a blog post announcing Fiona’s death. “We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore.”Fiona's story had captured international attention from the beginning. Born prematurely in January 2017, she weighed just 29 pounds and needed constant care from the zoo's team.Her survival became a remarkable story, attracting millions of followers who watched her grow into a healthy Nile hippopotamus.The Bengals also found their own way to remember her. Following the announcement of her death, players played the traditional military tribute song “Taps” inside their locker room.Higgins' sweatshirt added another personal moment to the tributes. articles.title: Josh Allen grew up around a fourth-generation farming business; how his family’s California roots followed him to Buffalo
articles.summary: Josh Allen is a fourth-generation farmer, and the family land in Firebaugh, California, still runs while he plays quarterback for the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body: Josh Allen is a fourth-generation farmer, and the family land in Firebaugh, California, still runs while he plays quarterback for the Buffalo Bills. His father, Joel, farms it with twin brother Todd. His great-grandfather came from Sweden in 1907. Allen spent his school years pulling weeds, driving tractors and working in his mother's restaurant long before the NFL. Those habits traveled east with him. They show up in how his family talks about him, and even in the melons that once made the trip from the Central Valley to Buffalo.Josh Allen grew up around a fourth-generation farming businessThe family story starts with Arvid Allen, a Swedish immigrant who came through Ellis Island in 1907. The Allens have farmed around Firebaugh since the Great Depression, in a town of roughly 8,000 people about 40 miles west of Fresno.Joel Allen is the third generation. His father and uncle started Allen Brothers Farming, and Joel and Todd took it over. Josh, the second of four kids, is the fourth.Sources disagree on the size. Some describe a 3,000-acre cotton farm. People reports that the extended family owns roughly 1,200 acres, growing cotton, wheat, grapes, melons and pistachios. Either way, it was big enough to need every pair of hands. Josh and his younger brother Jason weeded the family's cotton field. Joel has said his son drove the tractor, helped install irrigation, and was "not afraid of hard work."His mother, LaVonne, ran a restaurant in town, and he worked there too. Her own father owned a 3,000-acre farm in the Central Valley, so both sides of the household knew the calendar: plant, irrigate, harvest, repeat.Allen graduated from Firebaugh High in 2014, spent a year at Reedley College, then moved on to Wyoming before Buffalo took him seventh overall in 2018. Through all of it, the farm stayed the fixed point back home.How the California roots followed him to BuffaloDistance did not cut the connection. On draft night, Joel recorded a personal message for his son. His parents rarely miss games, the Los Angeles Times reported, and Firebaugh friends travel with them. Todd keeps a Josh bobblehead on his desk at the farm office. He told the paper, "No one works harder at his craft than Josh does."The farm has crossed state lines too. The Allens carried cantaloupe and honeydew melons from California to New York, a small, literal piece of home for Buffalo fans, according to Mexican outlet Excelsior. Josh Allen also has worked and invested on the family's Allen Ranch, and Wonderful Pistachios signed him as a partner, pointing to his pistachio-growing family.There is a reasonable reading here that goes beyond the feel-good angle. Farming punishes shortcuts and rewards patience. You do the work, then wait on weather and prices you cannot control. A quarterback faces something similar: a rep in practice pays off weeks later, if at all. That is my analysis, not a quote from Allen, but it fits the way his relatives describe him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Cris Collinsworth will miss this week's Sunday Night Football broadcast, but NBC already has a familiar face ready to take his place. Former Dallas Cowboys head coach Jason Garrett will join Mike Tirico in the booth for the Cleveland Browns vs. Las Vegas Raiders game on November 29.Collinsworth's absence has nothing to do with a permanent change to NBC's broadcasting team. The veteran analyst will work Thursday night's Thanksgiving clash between the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills before taking the rest of the weekend off. However, Sunday's assignment gives him another chance to work directly alongside Tirico during a nationally televised game.His coaching background could bring a different perspective to the broadcast. Garrett spent nearly a decade leading Dallas, where he worked with quarterbacks and managed some of the biggest names in the league. That experience could prove useful when the conversation turns to Cleveland's game plan and Las Vegas' rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.The Raiders selected Mendoza with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Meanwhile, Cleveland enters the matchup looking to strengthen its position in the AFC playoff race. The former Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver has worked NBC's Sunday Night Football broadcasts since 2009, making him one of the most familiar voices in the network's NFL coverage. His current contract also runs through the 2029-30 season, so Sunday's absence does not signal a permanent exit.NBC has used a similar Thanksgiving arrangement in recent seasons, allowing Collinsworth to work the holiday game before stepping away from Sunday's broadcast. articles.title: “What kind of player he is”: Aaron Rodgers issues strong reality check to Steelers’ front office as $132M DK Metcalf struggles and Max Hurleman delivers stunning performance
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has sent a pointed message to the Pittsburgh Steelers' front office after Max Hurleman stepped up when DK Metcalf was unavailable.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has sent a pointed message to the Pittsburgh Steelers' front office after Max Hurleman stepped up when DK Metcalf was unavailable. While the $132 million receiver continues to face questions over his production, Hurleman made his opportunity count against the Philadelphia Eagles. His impressive display caught Rodgers' attention, and the veteran quarterback now wants Pittsburgh's decision-makers to recognise what the young receiver brings to the team. Aaron Rodgers sends Steelers' front office a strong message after Max Hurleman's breakoutRodgers made his feelings clear during his postgame press conference following the Steelers' loss to Philadelphia. The quarterback praised Hurleman's performance but also directed his comments towards the people making roster decisions.“I think it’s as much for him as it is for everybody else upstairs making decisions,” Rodgers said.He then explained that Hurleman had already earned the respect of his teammates during training camp.“You know, I think everybody felt before the injury in camp that he was a 53 guy. I know the guys in our room did, for sure. So for him to go out there and finally get elevated and go out and play the way he played was not surprising to any of us, but great for his confidence and great reminder for the folks upstairs what kind of player he is.”Hurleman certainly gave Pittsburgh plenty to consider. He finished with six receptions for 61 yards and a touchdown, leading the Steelers in catches. He also contributed 68 combined yards on punt and kickoff returns, showing that he could help the team beyond his receiving duties.His biggest moment came late in the fourth quarter. With just 1:21 remaining, Hurleman caught a 20-yard touchdown pass from Rodgers to bring Pittsburgh within three points. The Steelers eventually lost 19-16, but the receiver had already made his case.Hurleman also earned an 81.4 PFF offensive grade, making him Pittsburgh's highest-graded offensive player against the Eagles. Even head coach Mike McCarthy praised his performance, particularly his route-running and work on special teams.However, his opportunity came under unusual circumstances.$132M DK Metcalf's struggles put more pressure on Steelers' receiving roomMetcalf's ejection against Philadelphia opened the door for Hurleman. The Steelers receiver got into an altercation with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean and appeared to poke him near the eye. Officials ejected Metcalf, leaving Rodgers without one of his primary targets.Although Metcalf avoided a suspension, his performance has raised questions. The four-year, $132 million extension he signed with Pittsburgh brought significant expectations, but his numbers have not consistently reflected his price tag.He has recorded 36 receptions for 434 yards and two touchdowns this season. His outing against Philadelphia was particularly disappointing, as he managed just one catch for two yards before his ejection.Rodgers also addressed the incident after the game, making it clear that the Steelers could not afford such mistakes.“Obviously we love DK, and I don't know what was going on out there, what was happening, but yeah, we can't have two of those (personal foul penalties),” he told reporters.Meanwhile, McCarthy explained that Hurleman's preseason injury against Buffalo had prevented him from securing a place on the initial 53-man roster. The coach believed the receiver deserved his opportunity and praised the way he handled his first extended NFL appearance.Despite that performance, Hurleman returned to Pittsburgh's practice squad after the game.That decision makes Rodgers' message even more interesting. The veteran quarterback has already seen what Hurleman can contribute when given an opportunity. With Metcalf struggling to deliver consistently, Pittsburgh has another receiver who deserves serious consideration.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Lions announce team owner Martha Firestone Ford dies at 101
articles.summary: Ford had been at least a partial owner of the team for more than 60 years before taking sole control in 2014 following her husband's death.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions announced Tuesday night that franchise owner and chair emeritus Martha Firestone Ford has died at 101.

Ford died at her home and was surrounded by family. She had been a part owner of the franchise for more than 60 years and took sole control after her husband's death in 2014.

She transitioned to emeritus status in 2020 and served in that role until her death. Ford and her late husband, William, purchased control of the Lions in 1963. The franchise had only been in Detroit for just 29 years at that point.

In recent years, as both owner and chair emeritus, Ford had supported her family in assuming a bigger role in running the team. She began to lean more on principal owner Sheila Ford Hamp, vice chair Martha Ford Morse, vice chair William Clay Ford Jr., and vice chair Elizabeth Ford Kontulis.

Philanthropy was hugely important to Ford, and throughout her life she always made sure to give back to the community.

"During her lifetime, Mrs. Ford expanded the Detroit Lions Charities and was a longtime trustee of Henry Ford Health. She held leadership positions with many organizations, including Merrill Palmer Skillman Institute, University Liggett School, Children's Home of Detroit and Edsel and Eleanor Ford House. She was also the founder and longtime board member of Henry Ford Maplegrove Center."

One of the highlights of Ford's tenure as owner was the remodel of Ford Field in 2017. She and the players also came together in 2019 to launch Detroit Lions Inspire Change, which is a social-justice initiative in Detroit.

In honor of the NFL's 100th season in 2019, Ford starred in the "A Lifetime of Sundays" documentary, which followed four matriarchs, including Ford, as their lives were highlighted with a focus on their impact on the game and their ties to historic teams.

The documentary also focused on Mrs. Virginia Halas McCaskey (Chicago Bears), Mrs. Patricia Rooney (Pittsburgh Steelers) and Mrs. Norma Hunt (Kansas City Chiefs).

Ford is survived by her four children, her 14 grandchildren and 17 great-grandchildren.

articles.title: Jay-Z’s Super Bowl halftime show is getting a historic Hollywood treatment; what NFL and music fans can expect
articles.summary: The Super Bowl is going to the movies.
articles.body: The Super Bowl is going to the movies. For the first time in the game's 61-year history, Super Bowl LXI will play live in IMAX theaters across the country, including Jay-Z's halftime show. The NFL, ESPN and Disney announced the plan on Monday, Nov. 23. The game kicks off Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. Hundreds of screens will carry a four-hour package that covers the pregame, the game, the halftime set and postgame coverage. It is also ESPN's first Super Bowl broadcast. Tickets go on sale in January, and the theater list is still to come.Jay-Z's Super Bowl halftime show heads to IMAX screensIMAX says this is the biggest live event it has ever carried, according to Variety. Theaters in the United States and select international markets will take part. The broadcast comes from ESPN's coverage at SoFi Stadium, so viewers get the same game as everyone at home. The difference is the room. A giant screen and cinema sound change how a halftime set lands, and Jay-Z's show is the obvious test case.Plenty of people watch the Super Bowl for the halftime show and care little about who lifts the Lombardi Trophy. For them, a seat in a dark theater with a stage production on a screen that size may beat a couch. Football fans get the stadium feel. Jay-Z fans get a performance at a quality usually saved for big film releases.Ken Potrock, Disney's president of major event integration, framed it as a shared experience. "Watching the Super Bowl with your fellow fans is one of the great shared experiences in sports, and this first-of-its-kind collaboration with the NFL and IMAX takes it to a historic new scale," he said in a statement.IMAX has tried live sports before, including Formula 1. The Super Bowl pulls a much wider crowd.Ticket dates, theaters and what to know before FebruaryTickets are expected to go on sale in January, about a month before kickoff. The theater list and ticket details are due in the coming weeks. Fans can sign up for updates on the IMAX website. Promotion starts early. Ads for the event are set to run in theaters this week, so Thanksgiving moviegoers may get the first look.The date adds a twist. Super Bowl Sunday lands on Valentine's Day in 2027, which gives couples a plan that suits both the football watcher and the person who wants a night out. Whether a four-hour cinema booking works as a date is another matter.This is SoFi Stadium's second Super Bowl and the ninth in the Los Angeles area. The Rams beat the Bengals 23-20 there in 2022. The first Super Bowl was played at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in 1967, so the league is returning to a city tied to the game from day one.Jay-Z takes the headline slot, and some of his fans may buy a ticket for those minutes alone.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Inside Olivia Culpo and Christian McCaffrey’s 49ers suite, where personalized M&M’s meet Christmas magic
articles.summary: Olivia Culpo has turned the San Francisco 49ers' private suite at Levi's Stadium into a holiday space, and she posted the whole process on TikTok.
articles.body: Olivia Culpo has turned the San Francisco 49ers' private suite at Levi's Stadium into a holiday space, and she posted the whole process on TikTok. The wife of running back Christian McCaffrey arrived with decorations, supplies and a stroller. The result: red M&M's carrying McCaffrey's initials, a football-themed tree and family photos on the shelves. The former Miss Universe set the clip to Brenda Lee's "Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree." Her caption was short: "Had way too much fun decorating this season." The clip has already passed 51,000 likes, and the details explain why.Inside Olivia Culpo and Christian McCaffrey's private 49ers suiteThe 49ers' scarlet and gold did a lot of the work, since those colors already look like Christmas. Culpo leaned into it everywhere. Wooden floating shelves now hold framed family pictures, wedding photos among them, plus two 49ers nutcrackers and a lit San Francisco logo.The counter is where the candy lives. Three glass jars with team branding hold gold-wrapped Hershey's Kisses, assorted chocolates and red M&M's carrying McCaffrey's initials and the 49ers logo. It's a small touch, but it says someone planned this suite for one specific family.Then there's the tree. It's small, set against the big windows that face the field, and it's packed with football ornaments, red berries, twinkling lights and a red-and-gold star with the 49ers logo. Culpo even slipped an instant photo between the branches. None of it looks showy, which helps.The less festive details may matter more. Culpo now brings motherhood into her game-day routine, and the suite shows it. She set up a portable playard and added children's activity books, a 49ers alphabet book and a team blanket. The fridge holds glass bottles of Coca-Cola. Put together, the room reads more like a family living room than a corporate hospitality space, which is probably the point for a couple whose Sundays revolve around football.Claire Kittle asks Culpo to decorate her suite nextTeammates' families noticed, too. Claire Kittle, who is married to 49ers tight end George Kittle, jumped into the comments with a simple request. "Okay come do ours next," she wrote. Culpo liked the comment, which had already picked up hundreds of likes of its own.The video itself has more than 51,000 likes. Fans seemed most taken with the child-friendly setup, not the tinsel. That tracks. Decorating a suite is easy to admire, but making room for kids at an NFL game takes actual planning.Kittle's note reads like a joke, but it also shows how far a good setup travels. Players' families spend many Sundays in these suites, so a room built around kids and family photos is bound to get noticed.Culpo's answer, at least in public, has been a like. Whether that turns into a second suite makeover is still open. The Kittles may have to wait.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Detroit Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford dies at 101; Inside her family’s longstanding grip on the franchise
articles.summary: Martha Firestone Ford, who owned the Detroit Lions from 2014 to 2020, died Tuesday at age 101.
articles.body: Martha Firestone Ford, who owned the Detroit Lions from 2014 to 2020, died Tuesday at age 101. She took charge at 88 after her husband, William Clay Ford, died, and she kept the team in the family when reports said the team might be sold. Her death comes two days before the Lions host the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. It will be the franchise's 87th Thanksgiving game, the most in NFL history. Ford went to every one of them for decades. Her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp, now runs the club and carries on what her mother started.Martha Firestone Ford dies at 101Ford was born Sept. 16, 1925, in Cleveland, the second child of Elizabeth Parke and Harvey Firestone Jr., who chaired the family tire company. Her grandfather, Harvey Firestone Sr., spent vacations with close friends Henry Ford and Thomas Edison. She later married into the Ford family. Her husband, William Clay Ford, was Edsel Ford's son. They wed in Akron, and per the Akron Beacon Journal, six police officers had to manage traffic outside the church.Football came later, through William. Martha listened to Lions games on a portable radio while Van Patrick called them. After William bought the team in full on Nov. 22, 1963, she started going to games with their four children. She never really stopped. She attended every Thanksgiving game, showed up at training camp and, well into her 90s, traveled to road games, riding shotgun in a golf cart through the stadium.Players noticed. “To have an owner that’s that hands-on, that wants to be around, you know she’s not an absentee owner,” said Miles Killebrew, a Lions safety from 2016-20. “I know the one thing is that Mrs. Ford cares and … I’ve been kind of spoiled by the fact that she definitely cares about the team. She wants us to do well.”A rocky six years in chargeHer path to ownership came late and without much warning. William died March 9, 2014, and reports said the Lions might be sold. After talking with commissioner Roger Goodell, Martha took over instead. She was 88. In “A Lifetime of Sundays,” the NFL's 2019 documentary, she recalled having “very mixed emotions” about it, “because I knew that I was missing the key person in my life. So I had a certain feeling of responsibility and wanting to do a good job.”The results were uneven. The Lions made the playoffs in her first season, then lost to Dallas after a controversial non-call. The next year opened 1-7. Ford fired president Tom Lewand and general manager Martin Mayhew, and the NFL sent adviser Ernie Accorsi to help with the search.Accorsi saw her in action. “She wasn’t going to be a custodian,” he said in the documentary.With Bill Belichick's blessing, Ford hired Bob Quinn as GM before the 2015 season and named Rod Wood president that November. Quinn later replaced coach Jim Caldwell with Matt Patricia, and the team went 6-10 in 2018 and 3-12-1 in 2019. Ford backed that pairing for one more year. “We expect to be a playoff contender,” she said. She stepped down June 23, 2020.What Hamp learned from her motherHamp's own start in football was not easy. In 1973, fresh from Yale, she asked NFL commissioner Pete Rozelle about a job. He told her there were none for women. “My mother really broke the ground for me,” Hamp said in 2020. “I look around the NFL and actually, there are quite a few women owners now.”Ford's hires failed, but her instinct to seek outside voices stuck with her daughter. The Detroit Free Press reported that William often let longtime GM Russ Thomas attend owners' meetings for him. Martha went herself and brought Hamp along. Hamp later built a search committee and landed Brad Holmes and Dan Campbell. The Lions are 56-38-1 under them, with playoff trips in 2023 and 2024 after a seven-year gap.“I’ve been an understudy to my mother,” Hamp said. “I mean, who gets to do that with their mother?”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers benched vs. Broncos; Steelers will start Mason Rudolph at QB instead
articles.summary: The future Hall of Fame quarterback may have played his final NFL game.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers announced Tuesday night that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback on Friday against the Denver Broncos. Rodgers will be inactive.

NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported after the announcement that the decision was head coach Mike McCarthy' s. There are no reports that Rodgers is dealing with an injury.

The Steelers didn't offer any explanation beyond a statement from team spokesman Burt Lauten announcing the roster move:

"The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for the game this Friday against the Denver Broncos. "Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for the game on Friday."

"The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for the game this Friday against the Denver Broncos.

"Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for the game on Friday."

Rodgers, a future Hall of Famer, may have played his last NFL game . He announced before the season started that this would be his last in the league. It's a stunning development for the 6-4 Steelers and a quarterback who is one of the best to ever play the game.

Rodgers, 42, is in his 22nd NFL season and well beyond his prime. He's in his second season with the Steelers, who hired McCarthy in the offseason in part because of his previous relationship with Rodgers.

McCarthy coached Rodgers for 13 seasons during Rodgers' prime and the pair won a Super Bowl together in Green Bay. Rodgers won two his four NFL MVP's while playing for McCarthy.

But with a playoff berth in the balance, McCarthy and the Steelers have decided 10 games into their season that Rudolph gives them a better chance at making the postseason.

McCarthy on Monday: 'Rodgers is our quarterback'

Tuesday's news drops one day after McCarthy gave Rodgers what appeared to be clear vote of confidence.

"Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback," McCarthy told reporters in his Monday news conference.

That statement came on the heels of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. The loss was the second straight for Pittsburgh and snapped a seven-game losing streak for an Eagles team that's been in a tailspin for most of the season.

Even with the consecutive losses, the Steelers remain on the right side of the playoff picture. If the postseason started this week, Pittsburgh would play as the final wild-card team and the No. 7 seed in the AFC.

Will Steelers be better off with Rudolph?

Rodgers had displayed continued signs of decline this year with statistically his worst career season. But there are worse starting quarterbacks in the NFL. And it's questionable whether Rudolph, an established NFL backup, gives the Steelers a better chance at winning.

In 10 starts, Rodgers has completed 60.9% of his passes for 6.2 yards per attempt and 224.1 yards per game with 16 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. The Steelers rank 23rd in total offense, 22nd in passing offense and 22nd in scoring offense with 21.4 points per game.

Rudolph is a seven-year NFL veteran in his sixth season with a Steelers team that selected him in the third round of the 2018 NFL Draft.

In 38 career appearances, Rudolph has completed 64.2% of his passes for 6.6 yards per attempt with 30 touchdown and 22 interceptions. He's made 19 career starts, but has never established himself as an NFL starter.

With their postseason hopes on the line against a stout Broncos defense, the Steelers are ready to give Rudolph another chance in favor of their aging future Hall of Famer.

articles.title: If Aaron Rodgers is done for the season, why are Steelers rolling with Mason Rudolph?
articles.summary: The questions facing Pittsburgh's medium- to long-term future: How do the Steelers weigh their playoff contention this year against their QB outlook longer t...
articles.body:
Standing just past the end zone of the Pittsburgh Steelers' training camp field on an August afternoon, Will Howard reflected on his offseason.

He'd dropped from 242 pounds to 230, he said. He wasn't battling the bone fracture on his hand that had slowed his rookie year. He was a year into learning his personnel, even if he was newer to head coach Mike McCarthy's offensive system. The Steelers' 2025 sixth-round pick admitted he was excited.

"I feel like it's been a long time since I've actually played real football," Howard told Yahoo Sports on Aug. 4. "And I think there's a lot of excitement around the Steelers and around, I feel like, me a little bit."

Howard appreciated the energy from fans flocking to training camp headquarters in Latrobe, Pennsylvania. But the Ohio State product was also realistic about buzz around the Steelers' younger quarterbacks.

"Makes me feel great, but at the same time, it's all anticipatory," Howard said. "I haven't really given them anything to truly cheer about. So I want to actually go out there and improve myself this year and give them something to really cheer about."

The Steelers announced at 11:10 p.m. local time Tuesday that 31-year-old Mason Rudolph would be the starting quarterback for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos.

"Aaron Rodgers," they added, "will be inactive for the game on Friday."

The primary oddity lies in the Steelers' current decision, which feels sudden and strangely timed on a short week to prepare for a complex Broncos defense.

But there also remains the questions facing Pittsburgh's medium- to long-term future: How do the Steelers weigh their playoff contention this year against their quarterback outlook longer term?

Playoff hopes complicate longer-term Steelers QB reality

It shouldn't surprise anyone that head coach Mike McCarthy would rather call plays for Rudolph, who has 38 games of NFL experience, including 19 starts, compared to Howard and Drew Allar at zero. Right now, the 6-4 Steelers sit seventh in the AFC with the final wild-card spot .

The 5-5 New England Patriots lost quarterback Drake Maye this season and, seemingly, their playoff promise with it. The 4-6 Houston Texans loom below New England — and also loom on the Steelers' schedule after the Broncos.

The Steelers need a quarterback who can keep receiver DK Metcalf in check, spark their run game and overcome protection deficits.

Perhaps Rudolph starts at least until that Sunday primetime game vs. Houston in Week 13, while playoff hopes live. And perhaps Pittsburgh's postseason outlook is rosier than its recent play in losses to the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles, given the relatively shallow state of the AFC compared to the NFC.

Either way, general manager Omar Khan may need to ask himself: How long should I chase a roster on track for a first-round playoff exit, rather than build a roster that's set up to threaten for years to come?

McCarthy waxed poetic at training camp about how much his younger quarterbacks were learning in meetings from Rodgers' reflections on footwork, reads and plays in this offensive system.

The Steelers' closest taste so far this year was in the preseason with Howard, Allar (a 2026 third-round draft pick) and Rudolph.

Their surrounding casts varied. But across three preseason games, Allar completed 55.6% of pass attempts for 351 yards and two touchdowns and Howard completed 66.7% for 229 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. Allar also rushed for a touchdown.

In one preseason game, Rudolph went 10-for-11 passing for 93 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions.

Rudolph was named Rodgers' backup when the 53-man roster came down.

But the question remained: Would the Steelers reach a point in their season when they want to evaluate the room more broadly before deciding how to approach the 2027 draft?

Rodgers had stated clearly that this is his last season. He was, at season's start, the Steelers' present but not their future.

articles.title: Giants lessons help Walker Snee put Paramus Catholic teammates first
articles.summary: As Paramus Catholic football chases a state title, Walker Snee leans on lessons from his New York Giants family to support his teammates.
articles.body:
PARAMUS - Walker Snee does not want to make this about him, even if he still wishes he was the one leading Paramus Catholic into MetLife Stadium for the Non-Public B football championship game against DePaul on Saturday morning.

This is still his team, the one for whom he was the starting quarterback for nine games before fracturing his right ankle in the second quarter, ironically in a 21-7 victory over DePaul during the regular season.

Snee is still Paramus Catholic's quarterback in mind and spirit, just not on the field.

It's a cruel twist of fate that he has been forced to accept - he will not get the chance to finish off his sophomore varsity campaign in the stadium where his grandfather, Tom Coughlin, commanded the sideline as head coach of the New York Giants and his father, Chris, was one of the NFL's best as a two-time Super Bowl champion by his side.

"I mean, it's been tough, and I know, at the end of the day, I'll be better than ever because of this," Snee told NorthJersey.com and The Record. "Teaches you, never take any opportunities for granted, and it sucks, because I worked as hard as I could, we all did, to get the No. 1 seed [in the Non-Public B playoffs]. And now that we're here, one win away from the championship, I can't play, it's something you have to learn from, and I will."

Yet instead of feeling sorry for himself, as difficult as it has been, Walker Snee has found a purpose with the Paladins.

He is embracing the emotional struggle of having to watch another quarterback, teammate Rowan Martin, lead the team he once led. Circumstances have forced the 16-year-old to learn what it means to be a good teammate while also dealing with the heartache of having the rug pulled out from under you three games from realizing a childhood football dream, and in the building where that fantasy was born.

See Giants' Jermaine Eluemunor host Thanksgiving turkey giveaway

Given his family's Giants legacy, Snee has to look no further than that for inspiration and a path forward.

In 1990, the Giants started 10-0 and they were 11-2 when Phil Simms broke his right foot. At the time, his 92.7 passer rating was tops in the NFC and fourth in the NFL, ahead of Hall of Fame quarterbacks Joe Montana and Dan Marino.

Just like that, Simms' season was over. Jeff Hostetler, his backup, took over and the Giants ultimately won Super Bowl XXV with one of the greatest defensive game plans in NFL history and when Scott Norwood's kick that would have won the game sailed wide right.

"When people introduce me as a two-time Super Bowl champion, I go, 'That sounds a lot better than one-time Super Bowl champion,'" Simms once told me. "So that season means a lot to me, too, and I learned how to appreciate that team and all we accomplished."

Even this season, Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury seven plays into Week 2, and surgery followed, meaning his second campaign in the pros that held such promise was over.

"It's an extremely challenging situation, and it's extremely challenging whether you are a 16-year-old young man or a 30-year-old professional, or anywhere in between," Matt Simms, Phil's son and Walker Snee's private quarterbacks coach, told NorthJersey.com and The Record. "You put all the time and effort and energy into becoming a really good football player, an impactful football player who is trying to do great things for your program, no doubt it feels like the rug has been swept up from underneath you. It's not an easy thing, but it is part of the game. It's also a reminder how you might not be The Guy out there, you can still be the guy who can make a tremendous impact out there on the team win and be successful. Like my father did in '90, like Walker is doing for Paramus Catholic."

With Snee at quarterback, Paramus Catholic won five games, including a signature win over Bergen Catholic, which was ranked No. 1 in New Jersey at the time and where he played as a freshman. He was injured two weeks later, finishing the 2026 campaign with nearly 1,800 yards of total offense with seven passing touchdowns and six rushing scores.

Paramus Catholic defeated St. John Vianney and Donovan Catholic by a combined score of 98-14 to reach the Non-Public B final for the second straight season. The Paladins lost to DePaul in the 2025 final.

Snee underwent surgery and immediately jumped into what he hopes is a three-month recovery. He is also ranked as one of the top high school baseball players in New Jersey as a pitcher/outfielder, but this year was all about his gridiron quest with the Paladins.

Early-morning and late-night throwing sessions with teammates helped accelerate Snee's learning curve at Paramus Catholic on and off the field.

"We were together all the time, and our goal was pretty simple: be one of the best teams in the state," Snee said. "So we got really close, and I can't say enough about my guys, that's what this is about. A.J. Lopez, Yahzir Sylvester, Nehki Martin, Josiah Tuccille, Cameron Thomas, Amaree Ervin, Feury Diaz-Rinaldi, I'm here for them. I'm excited for them, excited for the entire team to finish."

For a week post-surgery, Snee was unable to be on his feet. So he was forced to be away from the team until he received medical clearance to use a protective walking boot and a scooter to get around.

He has broken down film of upcoming opponents with Paramus Catholic coach Greg Russo, attending every practice and doing what he can to support and cheer their efforts.

"He's been awesome," Russo said of the 6-foot-3, 185-pound Snee. "You know, the outside world might see things a certain way, but I've told Walker, 'This is your team, you got us here,' and that goes for the quarterback just as it would a running back or a linebacker. It's a lot for a young kid, and you try to navigate that, and I think he's done a really good job."

Part of that comes with being on the same sideline Coughlin used to walk Saturday.

"I still have moments where I go blank and forget, 'Oh wait, I can't be out there,'" Snee said. "And that sucks, it really does. I want to be a good teammate. I'm going to do whatever I can to help Paramus Catholic. I can't play, but this is my team, and we've got one more game. Let's go win it."

articles.title: How Steelers' QB decision impacts Browns, AFC wild card picture
articles.summary: The Steelers announced late Nov. 24 they would be starting Mason Rudolph at QB this week. How does that impact the AFC wild card race?
articles.body:
BEREA ― There's a lot of variables that come into play when teams are chasing a playoff berth .

Obviously, the Browns' clearest path to the playoffs is for them to win games. Preferably a few of them not requiring last-minute drives to secure the victory.

However, there's other teams around the Browns who will also play their part in how the race shakes out. What those teams do can have an impact, directly or indirectly, on the Browns' fortunes.

Cleveland Browns vs Houston Texans. Best photos from Week 10 NFL game

The Pittsburgh Steelers made a decision late Nov. 24 that could be such a move. The Steelers, as The Ringer's Tom Pelissero first reported, are benching quarterback Aaron Rodgers and starting Mason Rudolph for their Black Friday home game against the Denver Broncos .

The Steelers have the same 6-4 record as the Browns do, but sit behind them in both the AFC North and AFC playoff standings because of tiebreakers. Cleveland is in second place in the division and No. 6 in the AFC, while Pittsburgh is in third place in the AFC North and No. 7 in the conference.

So, since quarterback is the most important position on the field, it's probably time to dive into the quarterback situations for the teams truly in the thick of the playoff race. The cutoff will be teams currently with four wins.

No. 6: Cleveland Browns (6-4), Deshaun Watson

Watson hasn't been great this season, but he's certainly played well enough to have the Browns in this spot. Of course, that's thanks to six fourth-quarter comebacks, five of those coming in the final two minutes. His play the first three quarters has been, at best, inconsistent.

No. 7: Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4), Mason Rudolph

The stunning late-night announcement that Rudolph will be starting for at least this week speaks to the general uncertainty around the Steelers' quarterback situation. It also speaks to how Rodgers had been playing overall, as well as some potential internal questions, that coach Mike McCarthy felt the need to go this route.

No. 8: New England Patriots (5-5), Tommy DeVito

Drake Maye's injury has put the Patriots' hopes in the hands of DeVito. Wait. Is that Daniel Jones' music you hear?

No. 9: Houston Texans (4-7), C.J. Stroud

If we're being honest, this is the best quarterback situation of the group. Stroud has played like a top-10-to-15 quarterback this season. The problem for the Texans is that loss to Watson and the Browns, which gives Cleveland a head-to-head tiebreaker.

No. 10, Las Vegas Raiders (4-7), Fernando Mendoza

Mendoza has had his moments. The No. 1 overall pick also has only had two career starts. Start No. 3 comes against the Browns on "Sunday Night Football," a game which could significantly impact both teams' playoff hopes.

No. 11: Baltimore Ravens (4-7), Jacoby Brissett

Brissett is the consummate pro. However, the Ravens would be in much better shape if Lamar Jackson and/or Tyler Huntley were healthy and available. Can Brissett win enough to keep Baltimore in the race until there's a chance Jackson could return later in the season?

articles.summary: Find out who is playing in the NFL Thanksgiving week games including the Rams-Packers Thanksgiving Eve matchup and holiday schedule.
articles.body:
NFL fans will enjoy a tripleheader on Thanksgiving Day, marking the century-long tradition established before the league even had its current name.

The league's tradition dates back to 1920, when it was still called the American Professional Football Association, and the date of Thanksgiving hadn't yet been written into federal law. The only years when games were not played were from 1941 through 1944, during World War II.

The Detroit Lions and the Dallas Cowboys play on Thanksgiving every year. The Lions began this tradition in 1934, playing every year from the 1939-1945 seasons due to the Great Depression and World War II. The Cowboys adopted the tradition later, in 1966, and have played every year except 1975 and 1977.

A third prime-time game on Thanksgiving Day was also added in 2006, played by teams other than the Lions and the Cowboys. In 2026, for the first time, two teams will be playing on Thanksgiving Eve, an addition that follows the 2023 introduction of the Black Friday game.

articles.title: Tennessee Titans make changes to practice squad
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans added defensive back Derrick Canteen to the practice squad while waiving two linebackers.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans not only held workouts and added a cornerback to the 53-man roster, but also made practice squad changes.

The Titans brought back defensive back Derrick Canteen, who has bounced on and off the practice squad all season, and waived linebacker Dominique Hampton in a corresponding move. The Titans also waived linebacker Milo Eifler from the reserve/injured list.

This move again reunites Canteen with Saleh, who were together with the San Francisco 49ers in 2025, after he signed as an undrafted rookie free agent following the draft. The 5-foot-10, 193-pound defensive back spent the majority of his rookie season on the 49ers' practice squad.

Canteen is a second defensive back who was brought in by Tennessee on Tuesday, joining former Carolina Panthers cornerback Corey Thornton, who is being added to the 53-man roster pending a physical.

Canteen should be at the facility on Wednesday when the Titans take to the field to start preparations for their Sunday matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: 2027 NFL mock draft 2.0: Jets get aggressive for a QB but it's not Arch Manning who is a top-3 pick
articles.summary: Like in my first mock draft of this season, I still have the Jets trading up to the top spot to get a quarterback. Step on up, Drew Mestemaker.
articles.body:
Here's another mock draft to help fill some time during your holiday travel.

And yes, like in my first mock draft of this season , I still have the Jets trading up to the top spot to get a quarterback.

1. New York Jets (Trade with Tennessee Titans) — Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State

In this deal, the Jets keep the No. 5 overall pick and package the Nos. 4 and 15 picks and a 2028 second-rounder to move up and tab Mestemaker as their QB of the future. Mestemaker has solid size (6-foot-3, 215 pounds) with a good but not overwhelming arm. He plays in a friendly offense that he maximizes with his aggressiveness. He's a loose athlete with a knack for changing arm slots and the arc on his throws. He's had some inconsistent play over the last month or so as his aggression leads to too many dicey decisions. Yet he's the exact type of gunslinger who would be fun to pair with the Jets' assortment of talented young skill players.

2. Los Angeles Chargers — Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

A season from hell can have its rewards!

3. Miami Dolphins — Arch Manning, QB, Texas

I kept Manning in the top 10 of my midseason big board . The shorthand version: he's been inconsistent, but I always come back more optimistic about him after reviewing his film with context in Texas' offense. I am still continuing to bet on Manning's athleticism, size, creativity and ability to navigate the pocket. The Dolphins are having an ideal tanking season of losing games, but they're competing with a well-schemed offense and defense with young players starting to shine on both sides of the ball. Manning would be dropped into a better-than-it-appears situation in Miami with the Dolphins' young and talented wide receivers (hello, Caleb Douglas!) and an already competent offensive line. Veteran center Aaron Brewer would help ease the learning curve, too.

4. Tennessee Titans (Trade with New York Jets) — Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina

Instead of snagging another wide receiver for the improving Cam Ward, now armed with three first-round selections, the Titans plan on finding a pass catcher later in a very good wide receiver class. I have an inkling they bet correctly in this mock, too. The Titans tab the über-talented Stewart, giving head coach Robert Saleh his new version of Nick Bosa to jump-start what has been the league's worst defense.

5. New York Jets — Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

Loaded already with skill players on offense and a Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate in David Bailey up front, the Jets take Moore to fill the hole left in the wake of the Sauce Gardner trade to the Colts. Moore has size and length packaged with top-end footwork and understanding of wide receiver routes. He can play inside and outside, and completely snuff out the opposition's No. 1 options. The Jets might end up getting an upgrade at corner.

6. Arizona Cardinals — Austin Simmons, QB, Missouri

Yes, the Cardinals went with Carson Beck in the third round in April, but they haven't really seen much of Beck so far to have the signal-caller spot solidified. Instead, the Cardinals go with one of the biggest risers this season to be their quarterback of the future. Simmons can spin the football. His aggression, arm talent and weekly improvement have his stock soaring this year, even if the box score numbers have been up-and-down. He re-signed with Missouri, but with a notable caveat that he is still free to gauge his draft stock . Pairing Simmons with Mike LaFleur in an offense that likes to have its quarterback drop straight back and work from the pocket has me excited about the fit.

7. Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana

The Buccaneers desperately need outside options with size to help pop open the offense, even with recent investments at the position. Ted Hurst was drafted in April as a Day 2 dart throw and Emeka Egbuka was drafted the year before that, but Egbuka has struggled with injuries while languishing in this year's morbid Buccaneers passing game. He also might be best as a power slot option in the future who does his best work against zone, like his teammate Chris Godwin Jr. was during his peak years. Becker gives the Buccaneers size (6-foot-4, 208 pounds), a ball winner and a valid deep threat to open up space for their running game and other receiving options. Now the ball just has to get to him.

8. New Orleans Saints — Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson

No more stopgaps for the Saints on the outside. No more Kool-Aid McKinstry being targeted by quarterbacks. Rejoice, Saints fans. Hampton is a big defender who can play in zone but might be best in man-to-man situations. He impacts the game with his size (6-foot-2, 205 pounds) and awareness, and would help solidify the outside cornerback spot for the Saints.

9. Philadelphia Eagles — Jordan Seaton, OT, LSU

Back to the basics of team-building for the Eagles. After a retirement and couple of trades that hit both sides of the ball, Philadelphia is looking to put beef back on the menu. So to the trenches the Eagles go, taking the talented Seaton to be up to the unenviable task of replacing Lane Johnson at right tackle.

10. Atlanta Falcons — Zereoue Williams, OT, Utah

I stewed on taking a quarterback for the Falcons. I then eyed a front-seven player like Chris Cole from nearby Georgia to inject even more talent into Atlanta's defense. But, do the Falcons pursue a veteran option at quarterback this offseason? Or do they really like a quarterback here, even if he's fourth off the board? Jalon Walker was a recent first-round selection with James Pearce taken in the same draft. Do the Falcons select another edge defender (Walker provides different skills than the others, but the question remains) with Colin Simmons still on the board? The Falcons could go with another wide receiver here, too, and I wouldn't fault them.

Instead, the Falcons give themselves a right tackle for next year and a potential left tackle replacement for when the immortal Jake Matthews hangs them up. Williams is twitchy and still developing his skillset playing the position, but he is an easy-moving athlete who can hang as a blindside protector for a long time if he continues to ascend as he has this season.

11. Baltimore Ravens — Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas

The Ravens could go in a variety of directions here and I would totally understand their decision. They instead bolster a position they just spent on in free agency. Simmons is an explosive athlete who is best when he can pin his ears back and get after the passer. Trey Hendrickson is still on the roster and Mike Green has had flashes. Simmons could give the Ravens another needle-moving talent to throw at quarterbacks.

12. Las Vegas Raiders — Jackson Harris, WR, LSU

Brock Bowers can lead a passing game as he's that kind of dynamic pass catcher. But the Raiders need more players to take advantage of Bowers' gravity, and also to help carry the load when he's injured. Harris has been a huge riser this season and is one of my favorite players in this draft. He's a strong-handed receiver who is smooth as a route runner and after the catch. Harris is useful for any type of offense and would complement Bowers perfectly.

13. Houston Texans — Lance Heard, OT, Kentucky

There's a couple of defensive options here that stared at me. The Texans go with Heard, a people mover in every sense of the word. Heard's physical style would fit perfectly in a Texans offense that has started to shift its attack to a more at-you run game.

14. Washington Commanders — Xavier Gilliam, DT, Tennessee

Wide receiver was also in play here for the Commanders, but perhaps Antonio Williams' recent play helped me lean elsewhere. The Commanders go with the explosive Gilliam to add to a defensive front that could lose Daron Payne in free agency this offseason. This will help bolster the spine of Washington's defense.

15. Tennessee Titans (Trade with New York Jets) — Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia

The Titans again provide reinforcements for the league's worst defensive unit. I went with Robinson over Mississippi State's Kelley Jones, despite Jones perhaps being a more traditional fit for what Robert Saleh and Gus Bradley like in their cornerbacks. Robinson is a twitchy player with ball skills. He's not the biggest, but he constantly makes plays on the ball with his burst and awareness.

16. New England Patriots — Trey'Dez Green, TE, LSU

I think this might be the only carryover I had from my first mock draft to this one. And my analysis doesn't really change much: Josh McDaniels likes his tight ends. Drake Maye likes throwing to his tight ends. The Patriots have to continue to add talent to their offense, so any position makes sense here. Hunter Henry turns 32 next month and has slowed down, even if he still is a solid player. Green is a massive target who looks and plays like the former basketball player that he is. He has excellent skills and has developed his strength, which has shown up as a blocker and when working through contact. He's also not stiff getting in and out of breaks and with the ball in his hands. Pairing him with 2026 third-round selection Eli Raridon would give the Patriots a massive tight end room with catching range and athleticism for Maye to fire throws to for years to come.

17. Cleveland Browns (via Los Angeles Rams) — LaNorris Sellers, QB, South Carolina

The Browns throw another dart at the quarterback position. And boy, what a chance of hitting bull's-eye this would be. Sellers is young (important to the Browns process) and has some of the loudest tools you'll ever see at the position. His play has felt more calm and decisive over the past month, but he will need more time, especially in a more conducive situation than the one he's been in the past few years. Landing in Cleveland with the Browns' exciting young group of pass catchers isn't the worst place to settle, especially with head coach Todd Monken, who has gotten the most out of his quarterbacks at multiple stops.

18. Seattle Seahawks — Chris Cole, LB, Georgia

This might be a "race to the podium" type pick for the Seahawks. I had Cole as the 10th overall player on my midseason big board. He's that type of impact player. His range is exceptional and he is constantly around the football. He could be the centerpiece for Mike Macdonald's defense for years to come.

19. Carolina Panthers — Greg Johnson, OG/C, Minnesota

OK, I lied. Here's another carryover from my last mock draft that I just can't help but like. Johnson would help solidify the interior of the Panthers' offensive line that has been ravaged by injuries this season. Johnson's best spot at the next level is center, but his positional versatility would be welcomed in Carolina.

20. Cleveland Browns — Boubacar Traore, Edge, Notre Dame

I peeked at another offensive lineman here, despite this year's Spencer Fano selection and hit on the Austin Barber pick. Funnily enough, I have compared Traore to Jared Verse (but might be leaning more toward a DeMarcus Lawrence comparison). Either way, those are two strong defenders who can push the pocket, and that's exactly what Traore brings to the table. He would be another strong edge defender to add to the Browns' front.

21. Pittsburgh Steelers — C.J. Carr, QB, Notre Dame

Carr is a heady player who constantly finds the right answers with the football. He is an accurate thrower with a quick and consistent throwing motion, a combination of attributes that will give him plenty of fans at the next level. Carr would be a clean fit with Mike McCarthy because of his quick decision-making and McCarthy's more traditional West Coast offense.

22. Dallas Cowboys (via Green Bay Packers) — Kelley Jones, CB, Mississippi State

Even with the Joey Porter Jr. trade and Daron Bland contract, the Cowboys want to inject even more talent into their defensive back room. Something up the defensive spine, at all three levels, could be in play here, too. I went with the long and rangy Jones to give the Cowboys another player to throw at the cornerback position.

23. New York Giants — Jadan Baugh, RB, Florida

The Giants have been itching to upgrade their running back room. They flirted with adding Jonathan Taylor at the trade deadline and even had a foray with Najee Harris this season. Baugh would immediately help the Giants' run game get back on track. He's not the most explosive athlete, but he has size (6-foot-1, 225 pounds) and runs with balance and patience to help his blockers out. He's a perfect back for a Greg Roman offense. I've compared him to a super-sized version of current Giants running back Devin Singletary.

24. Cincinnati Bengals — Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa, LB, Notre Dame

If you've watched the Bengals this year, a couple things stand out. Wow, that offense can score. And wow, the other offenses seem to complete a lot of passes between the numbers. Viliamu-Asa is a hammer who would give the Bengals physicality and more awareness over the middle of the field.

25. Philadelphia Eagles (via Jacksonville Jaguars) — Will Echoles, DT, Ole Miss

More beef for the Eagles! I almost went with another offensive lineman here. Instead, I went to the defensive side of the ball. Echoles is a uniquely built (6-foot-3, 315 pounds) but powerful defender who plays with quick hands. He is a disruptive player wildly different from Jordan Davis, winning with quickness and able to fulfill a variety of roles along the defensive front.

Chambliss or Darian Mensah were considered here. Chambliss is an atypically built quarterback with a unique background to match. He has arm talent and can put real RPMs on the football. Some of his best attempts are throws that he drove over the middle of the field on third down or in the red zone. He's had some shaky weeks recently but I think he's worth taking a chance on because of his work from the pocket and ability to create. And it's the Vikings who decide to take another stab at the position.

27. Kansas City Chiefs — Reed Harris, WR, Arizona State

The surprisingly competent play of Kahlil Benson has the Chiefs deciding to not look at tackle again in the first round. The Josh Downs trade has had promising early returns. Yet the Chiefs will look to add size with even more speed to the receiver spot. Harris is a vertical threat with ball skills and surprising bend given his large frame (6-foot-5, 220 pounds). He has been productive throughout the year and would give the Chiefs' offense an outside threat it has desperately needed for years.

28. Tennessee Titans (via Chicago Bears) — Nick Marsh, WR, Indiana

Marsh is a sure-handed option any quarterback would love to have. He can play inside and out, with real blocking chops to be featured as a power slot option. He has vertical ability, strong hands on the outside and has a feel working against zone. He would fit in any type of offensive scheme and would give Cam Ward another reliable option to grow with.

29. Detroit Lions — KJ Bolden, safety, Georgia

Bolden plays with his hair on fire and would be a perfect fit for the Lions under head coach Dan Campbell. With Brian Branch slated to hit free agency this offseason and Kerby Joseph recently returned from a knee injury, the Lions plop another impact player on the back end of their defense.

30. Denver Broncos — Tae Johnson, safety, Notre Dame

Johnson has battled a foot injury this year, but it looks like he will return soon . He is a hyperathletic and rangy defender who can impact the game in a variety of ways (watch his outing against Pittsburgh last year). Talanoa Hufanga is the only veteran starting safety signed through 2027, so Johnson fills a need while giving the Broncos' defensive backfield another dynamic player.

31. San Francisco 49ers — Trevor Lauck, OT, Iowa

"No, this is the draft where the 49ers will take an offensive lineman in the first round."

32. Buffalo Bills — Anthonie Knapp, OG, Notre Dame

Wide receiver seems to always be an option when discussing the Bills. A defensive back of some sort is another spot I looked at here. The Bills instead bolster their offensive line with Knapp to be their long-term option at left guard.
